entities.summary: William Stukeley was an English antiquarian, physician, and Anglican clergyman who pioneered the scholarly investigation of prehistoric monuments in England, particularly Stonehenge and Avebury. Born in 1667 in Holbeach, Lincolnshire, Stukeley was the son of a lawyer and worked in his father's law business before attending Saint Benet's College, Cambridge. In 1709, he became the rector of a small church in Lincolnshire, a position he held until his death in 1765. Stukeley's most notable work is 'The Antiquities of England, Vol. I: Stonehenge,' which was published in 1752 and remains a seminal text in the field of archaeology. He also wrote several other books on archaeology, medicine, and the natural sciences. Stukeley's contributions to the field of archaeology were significant, as he was one of the first scholars to approach the subject with a scientific and methodical approach. His work laid the groundwork for later archaeologists and continues to be studied and respected today.
